summary:
Generated at 2026-11-06T21:17:17Z, 17 minutes after the close, so every US equity, sector and theme number below is a settled 2026-11-06 close rather than an intraday snapshot. Total risk 68.90 stays in high_risk with the regime at risk_off for a 2nd consecutive session, down 2.50 points from 71.40 on 2026-11-05. That decline is not relief. Cross-asset fell from 87.50 to 50.00 and took 5.63 points out of the score as its three price-sensitive legs released with today's rebound, while volatility rose from 43.18 to 72.62 and put 4.42 points back, because the layer finally ingested the 2026-11-05 VIX close of 28.18 after reading 16.61 for a full session.

The session was the rebound after Thursday's violent selloff: 18 of 22 sector and theme rows closed higher with a mean of 3.08, led by quantum computing at 13.91, semiconductor equipment at 7.03, autonomous driving at 5.94 and AI infrastructure at 5.59, with AMD 11.04, MU 5.12, TSLA 4.23 and NVDA 2.78. The index split was wide: the S&P 500 rose 0.32, the Nasdaq 1.09 and the Dow fell 0.46 per the CLS relay, while SPY added 0.31 and IWM 0.98. The rebound recovered only part of the week: MU is still 22.01 lower on the week and AMD 11.05 lower, and 4 of the 8 cross-asset legs remain in stress. Credit never confirmed the equity selloff, with HYG down only 0.32 on 2026-11-05 against 4.41 for SPY, which is why the read stays high_risk rather than a liquidity liquidation.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Cross-asset confirmation fell from 0.875 to 0.5, with triggered legs dropping from 7 to 4, the largest single drag at 5.63 points. The three legs that released are the price-sensitive ones: the S&P proxy swung from 4.11 lower to 0.31 higher, copper from 2.81 lower to 0.17 higher and gold from 1.05 higher to 0.96 lower. Still firing are dollar strength, real-rate pressure, bitcoin weakness and small-cap underperformance, and the first two are level-type indicators that are independent of any single session.

Volatility rose from 43.18 to 72.62, adding 4.42 points in the other direction. The VIX input is now the 2026-11-05 close at 28.18 against 16.61 before, a 69.66 percent one-day rise at the 92.62 percentile, while 20 day realised volatility at 19.94 barely moved. Those 4.42 points describe Thursday's fear, not today's tape.

Liquidity and credit rose from 74.74 to 78.10, adding 0.67 points. High yield OAS widened from 3.32 to 3.48 at the 89.31 percentile and investment grade from 0.91 to 0.93, while overnight reverse repo at 0.15 is effectively drained. Credit widening is the one input that moved against the equity tape this week.

Equity structure fell from 81.20 to 71.47, a 1.95 point relief. On a 63 session window the new low share dropped from 0.5096 to 0.0892 and the share above the 200 day average edged from 0.2516 to 0.271, but the new high share fell from 0.0318 to 0.0191. The improvement is fewer lows, not more highs.

Macro was essentially flat at 73.98. The 2026-10 payrolls added 165 against 60 before and unemployment fell to 4.1 from 4.2, a clear beat; the 2026-09 CPI rose from 3.35 to 3.72 with the core at 2.57. Policy pricing has already turned to a hike: the FedWatch implied rate is 4.015 against an effective fed funds rate of 3.88.

supporting_signals.claim: The rebound was broad rather than a single-name squeeze: 18 of 22 rows rose with a mean of 3.08 and a median of 2.73. Only 4 declined, and all sit outside AI hardware: consumer electronics 1.41, cloud computing 0.49, gaming 0.23 and enterprise software 0.16.

All 5 tracked US single names closed higher, mean 4.78. AMD led at 11.04, ahead of MU 5.12, TSLA 4.23, NVDA 2.78 and AVGO 0.74; the semis leaders row at 4.92 is exactly the equal-weight mean of those four chip names.
Data quality supports the reading: all 7 input datasets are fresh, data quality is 1.0, coverage 0.93, consistency 0.8011, and confidence at 0.9322 is above the prior 4 sessions this week.

contradicting_signals.claim: Both risk_off limbs hold today (VIX 28.18 at or above 28, breadth 0.271 at or below 0.35), but both are the most reversible part of the read: VIX is Thursday's close, and the most stressed breadth measure already fell from 0.5096 to 0.0892. If the new low share holds, the regime call loses its justification even at an unchanged score.

The rates and FX vintages lag: the 10 year at 4.9 is the 2026-11-04 print and the dollar index at 121.6656 is still the 2026-10-30 reading, five sessions behind. The macro dimension at 73.98 therefore describes an older market than the rest of the layer.

The comparison baseline is a different basis: the 2026-11-05 generation was an intraday snapshot 23 minutes before the close while today is 17 minutes after it, so the 2.50 point day-over-day delta mixes a snapshot with a close and is not a clean one-day risk change.

what_changed_today: The layer was generated at 2026-11-06T21:17:17Z, 17 minutes after the close, so every US number is a settled close; the 2026-11-05 equivalent was an intraday price 23 minutes before the bell.

The total score is 68.90, down 2.50 from 71.40 on 2026-11-05; the published trend_1d reads 1.92 lower because it is measured against today's 17:50Z intraday generation at 70.82, whose same-day row was overwritten by this later write and cannot be cited as a day-over-day move.
Cross-asset fell from 87.50 to 50.00 as the S&P-down, copper-down and gold-up legs released, leaving 4 triggered. That is the largest single move in the score today.
Volatility rose from 43.18 to 72.62 because the VIX series filled in the 2026-11-05 print of 28.18, having read 16.61 for a full session.
Credit caught up: high yield OAS widened from 3.32 to 3.48 and investment grade rose from 0.91 to 0.93, both on the 2026-11-05 vintage.

The China block is still the 2026-11-05 settled session: all 11 A-share bars for 2026-11-06 carry open, high, low and volume but a null close, so the filter dropped them silently and the layer republished the prior session (7 of 11 higher, mean 0.17). That is not today's China move and is not quoted as one here.
The dollar index print is still pinned at 2026-10-30, five sessions behind, and rates are at 2026-11-04, two sessions behind.
watch_next: CPI on 2026-11-10 at 13:30Z is the next macro test. The real rate at 2.64 already sits at the 97.91 percentile and the 10 year at 4.9 at 96.63, so a hot print pushes both percentiles higher at once.
Whether volatility holds near 28.18, the source of today's 4.42 points. If VIX returns toward 16.61 the volatility dimension falls to 44.43 and the score gives up 4.23 points without any equity move.

Credit is the highest-leverage falsifier: high yield OAS at 3.48 is only 0.52 short of the 4 threshold, and clearing it would lift liquidity and credit and the widening leg inside cross-asset together.

The 4 legs still firing (dollar, real rate, bitcoin, small caps) are worth 7.50 points together, which is the entire remaining room for relief, and the bitcoin leg is only 0.16 lower, the easiest to flip.

Two things first next session: whether the 2026-11-06 A-share closes populate at all, since the null close has now dropped the China leg for a second session, and whether the volatility dimension gives back once the 2026-11-06 VIX print lands.

bull_case.title: Bull case: volatility mean-reverts
points: VIX 28.18 is the 2026-11-05 print and the tape has already turned (SPY 0.31, AMD 11.04, quantum computing 13.91). Were VIX back near 16.61 the indicator score returns to 39.76, the volatility dimension falls to 44.43 and the score gives up 4.23 points.
Cross-asset released 3 legs in a single session, and the remaining 4 are worth 7.50 points, the largest reserve of further downside for the score.
Credit never confirmed: high yield OAS at 3.48 is still 0.52 below the 4 threshold, so the episode reads as valuation compression rather than a solvency repricing.

base_case.title: Base case: the score holds in the 65 to 75 band
points: The score is 68.90 with confidence at 0.9322 and all 7 input datasets fresh, which is unusually well supported for a high_risk state.

Of today's four material moves, two are vintage catch-ups rather than fresh shocks: volatility 4.42 from Thursday's VIX and credit 0.67 from Thursday's spreads, while the other two, cross-asset 5.63 and equity structure 1.95, are today's tape.
Rates are two sessions stale at 4.9 and the dollar five sessions stale at 121.6656, so the macro dimension at 73.98 is more likely to be revised than to move on its own.

bear_case.title: Bear case: credit confirms and the score clears 71 again
points: A move through the 4 threshold on high yield OAS (currently 3.48, only 0.52 away) would do two things at once: liquidity and credit would rise from an already elevated 78.10 and the widening leg inside cross-asset at 50.00 would re-trigger.
The new low share at 0.0892 has the most room to reverse; a return toward 0.5096 would put equity structure back above 81.20, worth roughly 1.95 points.

VIX at 28.18 already sits at the 92.62 percentile, so a second shock lands on a dimension with almost no room left, and the real rate at 2.64 sits at the 97.91 percentile, leaving the macro side without a buffer either.
